entities.name: Stanislovas Kęsgaila
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Stanislovas Kęsgaila (Stanisław Janowicz Kieżgajło; d. 1527) was a powerful Lithuanian magnate of the Kęsgaila family, holding high offices including Samogitian elder and castellan roles that made his house a pillar of the Grand Duchy’s western governance. The Kęsgailos amassed estates and church patronage across Samogitia and Lithuania proper in the Jagiellonian era.

As elders of Samogitia they mediated between local Baltic society, Christianisation aftermath, and the Vilnius court—vital after the Thirteen Years’ War and Muscovite pressures. Magnate oligarchy increasingly structured politics beside the grand dukes.

Stanislovas represents the apex of Kęsgaila influence in early sixteenth-century Lithuania.

entities.summary:
Stanislovas Kęsgaila (alternate catalog slug stanislovas-ksgaila) denotes the same Kęsgaila magnate network of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania—Samogitian elders and castellans whose offices knitted Baltic provinces to Vilnius under the Jagiellonians. Parallel name spellings in Latin, Polish, and Lithuanian sources (Kieżgajło, Kęsgaila, Kiesgałło) often fracture into duplicate catalogue entries.

Historically the family dominated Samogitian administration, church presentation, and estate complexes that underwrote military service. Their prominence illustrates how orthographic variance in borderland elites can split modern knowledge graphs.

Treating this slug clarifies a duplicate pathway into Kęsgaila political history.
